column2: it goes to the ocean, becoming sevenfold, best of Brahmins. Chakshu, passing all the western mountains,
follows the western varsha called Ketumala to the ocean; Bhadra likewise crosses the northern mountains and the northern Kurus
and reaches the northern ocean, best of Brahmins. Extending to Nila and Nishadha are Malyavan and Gandhamadana;
between them stands Meru, shaped like the pericarp of a lotus; the Bharatas, Ketumalas, Bhadrashvas and Kurus
are the petals of the world-mountain, outside the boundary mountains. Jathara and Devakuta are the two boundary mountains,
extending north and south to Nila and Nishadha; Gandhamadana and Kailasa are the two, east and west,
eighty yojanas long, situated within the ocean. Nishadha and Pariyatra are the two boundary mountains,
extending north and south to Nila and Nishadha; on the western side of Meru they stand as the former two do.
Trishringa and Jarudhi are the two northern varsha mountains, extending east and west, situated within the ocean.
Thus these boundary mountains have been told by me, Brahmins, standing at Jathara, two to each of Meru's four sides.
The Kesara mountains that were spoken of on Meru's four sides, Shitanta and the rest, are exceedingly lovely.
The valleys between the mountains are frequented by Siddhas and Charanas; in them are very lovely forests and cities,
and excellent temples of Lakshmi, Vishnu, Agni, Surya, Indra and other gods, best of sages, resorted to by men and Kinnaras.
Gandharvas, Yakshas, Rakshasas, Daityas and Danavas play day and night in those lovely mountain valleys.
These are remembered as earthly heavens, abodes of the righteous, Brahmins; evildoers do not go there even in hundreds of births.
In Bhadrashva the Lord Vishnu dwells as Hayashiras (Horse-head), Brahmins; in Ketumala as Varaha; in Bharata bearing the form of the Tortoise;
and Govinda in the form of a Fish, eternal, dwells among the Kurus. In the universal form everywhere, Hari, all, Lord of all,
the support of everything, dwells, Brahmins, as the self of all. In the eight varshas beginning with Kimpurusha, best of Brahmins,
there is no grief, effort or anxiety, nor hunger, fear and the like; the people are well, free from affliction, devoid of all suffering.
They live a firm lifespan of ten or twelve thousand years. In these, Brahmins, there are not the other earthly things such as hunger and thirst.
In those places there is no reckoning of Krita, Treta and the rest. In all these varshas there are seven family-mountains each, and hundreds of rivers born from them, best of Brahmins.
Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Shudras in the middle, in their respective parts, are established with livelihoods of sacrifice, war, trade and the like.
The Shatadru, Chandrabhaga and others issue from the foot of the Himalaya; Vedasmriti and others from Pariyatra, sage.
The Narmada, Surama and others are rivers issuing from the Vindhya; the Tapi, Payoshni, Nirvindhya, Kaveri and others;
these born at the foot of Riksha are heard to remove sin; and the Godavari, Bhimarathi, Krishnaveni and others,
rivers born at the foot of Sahya, are remembered as removers of fear of sin; Kritamala, Tamraparni and others rise from Malaya;
Trisandhya, Rishikulya and others are remembered as born of Mahendra; Rishikulya, Kumara and others arise at the foot of Shuktimat.
Of these there are tributaries and thousands of other streams. Along them live these peoples: those of Kuru, Panchala, the Middle Country and others,
those of the east and the dwellers of Kamarupa, the Paundras, Kalingas, Magadhas, and the southerners everywhere,
and the western ones, Saurashtras, Shudras, Abhiras, Arbudas, Marukas, Malavas and the dwellers of Pariyatra,
Sauviras, Saindhavas, Shalvas, the dwellers of Shakala, Madras, Arama, Ambashthas, Parasikas and others.
They drink the water of these rivers and always live by the rivers, fortunate one, joyous and well-fed, crowded together.
In the Bharata varsha, great sage, the yugas occur: Krita, Treta, Dvapara and Kali; elsewhere nowhere.
Here ascetics perform austerity, sacrificers offer oblations, and gifts are given with devotion for the sake of the other world.
In Jambudvipa the Sacrifice-Person is always worshipped by men; in other continents Vishnu consisting of sacrifice is worshipped by other means.
Even here, great sage, Bharata is the best in Jambudvipa, for this is the land of action, while the others are lands of enjoyment.
Here, after thousands upon thousands of births, a creature sometimes gains human birth, accumulating merit.
The gods sing songs: "Blessed are those who, in that part of the land of Bharata, the cause of the abodes of heaven and liberation, are born again as human men.
Renouncing actions, whose fruits are not willed, in Vishnu of the form of the Supreme Self, they reach that land of action and, pure, merge into the Infinite.
We do not know when, with action that gives heaven exhausted, we shall obtain embodiment; blessed indeed are those humans who in Bharata are free of the senses' hold."
Thus the nine varshas of this Jambudvipa, a hundred thousand yojanas wide, have been told by me in brief, Brahmins.
Encircling Jambudvipa, the Milk-ocean stands outside, ring-shaped, a hundred thousand yojanas wide, Brahmins.
Thus Plakshadvipa has been described to you by me in brief, best of sages; now hear again of Shalmala.
The lord of Shalmala was the hero Vapushman; his sons, Brahmins, gave their names to the seven varshas:
Shveta, Harita, Jimuta, Rohita, Vaidyuta, Manasa and Suprabha, best of Brahmins.
The Shalmala continent is surrounded on all sides by the sugar-cane-juice ocean, twice as wide.
There also seven mountains, sources of jewels, should be known, which mark out the varshas, and likewise seven rivers.
Kumuda, Unnata, third Balahaka, Drona where the great herbs are, that is the fourth mountain,
Kanka the fifth, Mahisha the sixth, and Kakudman the seventh, the best mountain. Now, Brahmins, the names of the rivers:
Shroni, Toya, Vitrishna, Chandra, Shukra, Vimochani, and Nivritti the seventh; these are remembered as bringing peace from sin.
Shveta, Lohita, Jimuta, Harita, Vaidyuta, Manasa and Suprabha is the seventh name.
These seven varshas are endowed with the four varnas, and the Brahmins who live in Shalmala in these —
the Kapila, Aruna, Pita and Krishna, respectively Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras — worship him.
The sacrificers, with the best of rites, worship the Lord Vishnu, the imperishable Self of all, who has become Vayu and abides in sacrifice.
The presence of the gods is very pleasing there, and the great Shalmali tree gives its name to the place.
This continent is surrounded by the ocean of wine, equal in all directions to the width of Shalmali.
The wine-water ocean is surrounded on all sides by Kushadvipa, twice the width of Shalmala.
In Kushadvipa, hear of the sons of Jyotishman: Udbhida, Venuman, Svairatha, Randhana, Dhriti,
Prabhakara and Kapila; the order of varshas bears their names. In it live humans along with Daityas and Danavas,
and likewise gods, Gandharvas, Yakshas, Kimpurushas and others; there too the four varnas are intent on their own duties:
Damina, Shushmina, Sneha and Mandaha, best of Brahmins: Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras, named in order.
By performing the prescribed actions for the exhaustion of their own claims, in that Kushadvipa they worship Janardana in Brahma-form,
exhausting the intense duty that gives the fruit of authority. Vidruma, Hemashaila, Dyutiman, Pushtiman,
Kusheshaya, Hari and the seventh, Mandarachala: these are the seven varsha mountains in that continent, best of Brahmins.
There are seven rivers; I shall tell their names in order: Dhutapapa, Shiva, Pavitra, Sammati,
Vidyut, Ambhas and Mahi: these remove all sin. There are thousands of other small rivers and mountains.
In Kushadvipa there is a clump of kusha, whence its name. Of that measure the continent is surrounded by the ocean of ghee,
and the ghee ocean is surrounded by Krauncha-dvipa. Best of sages, hear of another, great Krauncha-dvipa,
whose width is twice that of Kushadvipa. In Krauncha-dvipa the great-souled Dyutiman had seven sons.
The great-minded one made the varshas bear their names: Kushaga, Mandaga, Ushna, Pivara, Andhakaraka,
Muni and Dundubhi: these seven are his sons, Brahmins. There too they are served by gods and Gandharvas, very lovely.
Best of sages, their names are: Krauncha, Vamana, third Andhakaraka,
Devavrata, Dhama, and another, Pundarikavan, and the great mountain Dundubhi; each is twice the one before.
Continent to continent the mountains and continents are thus; in these lovely varshas and best of varsha mountains,
the people live without fear along with hosts of gods, plentiful and fortunate, famed, best of Brahmins:
Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras, named in order. There are rivers, best of sages, which they always drink:
seven chief ones and hundreds of other small ones: Gauri, Kumudvati, Sandhya, Ratri, Manojava,
Khyati and Pundarika: these seven are the varsha rivers. There too by the varnas, Puskara and others, the Lord Janardana
is worshipped in Rudra-form by meditation and yoga near the sacrifice. Krauncha-dvipa is surrounded by the ocean of curd-whey,
equal in measure to Krauncha-dvipa on all sides; the curd-whey ocean is surrounded by Shakadvipa,
twice the width of Krauncha-dvipa, best of Brahmins. Of the lord of Shakadvipa, the great-souled Bhavya,
there were seven sons; he gave them seven varshas: Jalada, Kumara, Sukumara, Manirak,
Kusumoda, Modaki and the seventh Mahadruma. The seven varshas there too bear their names in order.
There too are seven mountains marking off the varshas: in the east, Udayagiri; another, Jaladhara;
then Raivataka, Shyama and Ambhogiri, Brahmins; Astikeya, the lovely Kesari, the best mountain.
The great tree there is the Shaka, frequented by Siddhas and Gandharvas, by contact with whose leaf-breeze supreme joy arises.
There the holy countries, endowed with the four varnas, are inhabited by great-souled ones, fearless and free of disease.
The rivers there are very sacred, removers of all fear of sin: Sukumari, Kumari, Nalini, Renuka,
Ikshu, Dhenuka, and Gabhasti the seventh; there are tens of thousands of other small rivers, best of Brahmins,
and mountains by the hundreds and thousands. Those who dwell in Jalada and the rest drink them joyfully.
In the varshas the countries are joined with the fourth aim (liberation); the very sacred rivers here, coming from heaven, reach the earth.
There is no loss of dharma there, nor excitement, nor grief; nor is there transgression of limits in those seven countries.
The Magas, Magadhas, Manasas and Mandagas: the Magas are mostly Brahmins, the Magadhas Kshatriyas,
the Manasas Vaishyas, and the Mandagas should be known as Shudras. Those who live in Shakadvipa worship Vishnu, Hari, in the form of the Sun,
properly with the prescribed rites by self-controlled persons. Then Shakadvipa, Brahmins, is surrounded all around by the Milk-ocean,
like a ring of the same measure as Shakadvipa; and the Milk-ocean, Brahmins, is surrounded on all sides by the continent called Pushkara,
twice as wide as Shakadvipa. In Pushkara, Savana's son was Mahavita.
Dhataki was the other; thus two varshas are named: Mahavita and another called Dhatakikhanda.
One famed varsha mountain there, fortunate ones, named Manasottara, lies in the middle, ring-shaped,
fifty thousand yojanas high, and just as wide, round on all sides.
It stands as though dividing in the middle the ring of Pushkara-dvipa; by it the two varshas are separated.
Each is ring-shaped, with the great mountain in their middle; humans there live ten thousand years,
free of disease, free of grief, free from attachment and aversion. There is no lowest or highest there, nor slayer and slain, Brahmins;
no envy, malice, fear, anger, fault, greed and the like. Mahavita is outside, Dhatakikhanda within,
of the Manasottara mountain, frequented by gods, Daityas and others. In the continent called Pushkara there is neither truth nor falsehood,
nor rivers or mountains in the continent with two varshas; humans are of equal dress and, like gods, of one form.
It is without the duties of varnas and ashramas, free from the removal of dharma, without the three Vedas, trade, law and service.
The two varshas then, Brahmins, are this excellent earthly heaven; time is pleasant to all, free from old age and disease.
In Pushkara, Dhatakikhanda and Mahavita, Brahmins — the banyan in Pushkara-dvipa is the best abode of Brahma;
in it Brahma dwells, worshipped by gods and Asuras. Pushkara is surrounded by the ocean of sweet water,
equal in width to Pushkara's circle. Thus the continents are surrounded by oceans, seven and seven.
Continent and ocean are equal, each next twice as large; the waters in all oceans are always equal.
There is never any deficiency or excess in them. As water in a pot placed on fire swells from contact with fire,
so, with the moon's increase, the water in the oceans, best of sages, rises and falls, neither less nor more.
With the moon's rising and setting, in the bright and dark fortnights, five hundred and ten fingers' breadth
of increase and decrease of the ocean waters is seen, best of Brahmins. Food in Pushkara-dvipa comes of itself,
and the people there always eat food of six flavours, Brahmins. All around the sweet-water ocean the arrangement of the world is seen:
a golden land twice as large, devoid of any creatures; then the mountain Lokaloka, ten thousand yojanas wide,
and as many thousands high, extending all around. Then darkness, covering that mountain, stands on all sides,
and the darkness is enclosed all around by the egg-shell. This earth, best of Brahmins, is fifty crore (yojanas) wide,
together with the egg-shell, with continents and mountains; this earth, supporter and creator, surpassing all beings in qualities, is the support of all the worlds, best of Brahmins.
Each nether world is ten thousand (yojanas), best of sages: Atala, Vitala, Nitala, Sutala,
Talatala, Rasatala, and Patala the seventh. Their soils are black, white, red, yellow, pebbly, rocky and golden,
where, best of Brahmins, there are fine palaces; in them hundreds of races of Danavas and Daityas live,
and kin of great Nagas. Narada said the nether worlds are lovelier even than the heavenly world;
after going from the nether regions to heaven he said in the assembly of heaven: where bright, radiant jewels give delight,
adorned with the ornaments of serpents — what is equal to Patala? Beautified here and there with Daitya and Danava maidens,
who does not feel pleasure in Patala, even one who is liberated? Where the sun's rays by day give light but not heat,
and the moon's at night gives only light, not cold, the serpents intoxicated with food, drink and great drinking,
where time is not known to the Danavas and others even as it passes; forests, rivers, lovely lakes and lotus-ponds,
the songs of cuckoos and the like, charming garments, very lovely ornaments, perfumes and unguents,
the sounds of lutes, flutes and drums are there always, Brahmins; these and other lovely things, objects of enjoyment by fortune, are enjoyed by Danavas,
Daityas and serpents who range in the nether regions. Beneath the nether worlds lies Vishnu's tamasic form
called Shesha, whose virtues Daityas and Danavas cannot tell, the Ananta praised by Siddhas, worshipped by gods, gods and sages;
manifest with a thousand heads, adorned with the spotless svastika, lighting the quarters with a thousand hood-jewels;
he makes all the Asuras powerless for the world's good, with eyes rolling with intoxication, always with a single earring,
crowned and garlanded, shining like a white mountain with fire; clad in blue, flushed with intoxication, adorned with a white necklace;
like the supreme mountain Kailasa with the Ganga falling with clouds, the tip of his hand resting on a plough, bearing an excellent pestle,
served in person by Kanti and by Varuni in bodily form; at the end of the kalpa, from whose mouths, blazing with flames of poison fire,
Rudra, whose nature is Sankarshana, emerges and devours the three worlds. He bears the whole orb of the earth made into a peak.
Shesha, worshipped by all the gods, dwells at the base of Patala; his valour, power, nature and form
cannot be described or known even by the thirty gods; the whole earth, on the red crest of his hood-jewels,
rests like a flower-garland; who will tell his valour? When Ananta yawns with eyes rolling in intoxication,
then this earth shakes, with its mountains, waters and many forests; Gandharvas, Apsarases, Siddhas, Kinnaras, serpents and elephants
do not reach the end of his virtues; therefore he is Ananta, imperishable, whose Hari-sandal is smeared by the hands of Naga women,
and, repeatedly blown by his breath, becomes a covering for the quarters. Having worshipped him, the ancient sage Garga learned the luminaries truly
and the whole fruit read in omens. By that best of Nagas the earth is held on his head; he bears all the worlds with gods, Asuras and humans.
A man who kills a bee, or destroys a village, goes to Vaitarani; those who drink semen and the like and break boundaries
go to Krichchhra, as do the impure and those who live by fraud. One who cuts forests in vain goes to Asipattravana.
Sheep-keepers and deer-hunters fall into the flames of fire; they go there, Brahmins, as does one who sets fire in cooking places.
